authoredSolutions.51: With \(\overrightarrow{AC}=\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{AD}=3\hat i+6\hat j+(\lambda-5)\hat k\), the projection of \(\vec v=\hat i+\hat j+\hat k\) is \(\frac{|\vec v\cdot\overrightarrow{AC}|}{|\overrightarrow{AC}|}=\frac{|4+\lambda|}{\sqrt{45+(\lambda-5)^2}}=1\). Squaring: \(16+8\lambda=70-10\lambda\Rightarrow\lambda=3\). Then \(9x^2-18x+5=0\) gives \(x=\frac53,\frac13\), so \(\alpha=\frac53,\beta=\frac13\) and \(2\alpha-\beta=\frac{10-1}{3}=3\).

authoredSolutions.58: For \(x\ge-2\): \(x^2+7x+16=0\) (no real root). For \(-4\le x<-2\): \(x^2+x+4=0\) (no real root). For \(x<-4\): \(x^2+7x-4=0\Rightarrow x=\frac{-7-\sqrt{65}}{2}\approx-7.53\) only (the other root fails \(x<-4\)). Exactly \(1\) real solution.
authoredSolutions.59: Differentiating \(6\int_1^x f\,dt=3xf(x)+x^3-4\): \(6f=3f+3xf'+3x^2\Rightarrow f'-\frac fx=-x\). With IF \(=\frac1x\), \(\frac fx=-x+C\), i.e. \(f=-x^2+Cx\). \(x=1\) gives \(f(1)=1\Rightarrow C=2\), so \(f(x)=2x-x^2\). Then \(f(2)-f(3)=0-(-3)=3\).
authoredSolutions.60: Substituting \(y=\frac{1-\alpha x}{2}\) into \(x^2-9y^2=9\): \((4-9\alpha^2)x^2+18\alpha x-45=0\). No intersection needs discriminant \(<0\): \(720-1296\alpha^2<0\Rightarrow\alpha^2>\frac{5}{9}\approx0.556\). Among the choices only \(\alpha=0.8\) satisfies this.
authoredSolutions.62: Circle 2 has centre \((2,1)\), radius \(3\); the centres are \(\sqrt{34}\) apart. Two distinct intersections require \(|r-3|<\sqrt{34}<r+3\), i.e. \(r\in(\sqrt{34}-3,\sqrt{34}+3)\). Thus \(\alpha\beta=(\sqrt{34})^2-9=34-9=25\).

authoredSolutions.69: Homogeneous: with \(y=vx\), \(x\frac{dv}{dx}=\sqrt{1+v^2}\Rightarrow\sinh^{-1}v=\ln x+C\). \(y(1)=0\Rightarrow C=0\), so \(v+\sqrt{1+v^2}=x\), giving \(y+\sqrt{x^2+y^2}=x^2\) and \(y=\frac{x^2-1}{2}\). Hence \(y(3)=\frac{9-1}{2}=4\).
